posts.text:
Morgan Housel (quoting Warren Buffett), in The Psychology of Money.
At the 2013 Berkshire Hathaway shareholder meeting, Buffett said he had owned roughly 400–500 stocks over his career and made most of his money on about 10 of them. Charlie Munger followed up by noting that removing just a few of Berkshire’s top investments would leave its long-term record pretty average.

In my opinion, the key to outperforming is being able to find those 10 key stocks early in life.  

Like Buffett, stick with them over the long run.  Typically accumulating them when they drop back to longer term major moving averages.  There’s no substitute for having core positions in quality growing businesses that will become household names. 

I’ve also always loved to combine this thinking with Peter Lynch’s philosophy of investing it in products you love.  Trouble is, often by the time if discovered a new great product the stock was already expensive or unavailable as a fully funded private.   (I missed Lulu lemon like this… but just)
